title: If Earth stopped spinning, you would not stop

beats.say: If Earth suddenly stopped spinning, you would not stop. You would keep flying east at 1,674 kilometres per hour.
beats.speak: If Earth suddenly stopped spinning, you would not stop. You would keep flying east at one thousand six hundred and seventy four kilometres per hour.

head: WHY THAT
NUMBER?
beats.say: Earth is 40,075 kilometres around the equator, and it turns once every 23.93 hours. Divide one by the other.
beats.speak: Earth is forty thousand and seventy five kilometres around the equator, and it turns once every twenty three point nine three hours. Divide one by the other.

head: 465 METRES
EVERY SECOND.
beats.say: That is 465 metres every second. Faster than the speed of sound.
beats.speak: That is four hundred and sixty five metres every second. Faster than the speed of sound.

head: THE AIR
KEEPS GOING TOO.
beats.say: And the air does not stop either. The strongest gust ever measured was 408 kilometres per hour. This wind is four times faster.
beats.speak: And the air does not stop either. The strongest gust ever measured was four hundred and eight kilometres per hour. This wind is four times faster.

head: NOW WALK
NORTH.
beats.say: But it depends where you stand. At 45 degrees north, halfway to the pole, it is 1,184.
beats.speak: But it depends where you stand. At forty five degrees north, halfway to the pole, it is one thousand one hundred and eighty four.

head: AND AT THE
NORTH POLE?
beats.say: And at the North Pole? Zero. You would just stand there and watch everyone else leave.

head: 1 DAY.
1 YEAR.
beats.say: And if it never started again, one day would last a whole year. About six months of sunlight, then six months of night.

head: RELAX.
IT WON'T.
beats.say: Relax. Earth is slowing down, but tides only add 1.7 milliseconds to the day every century.
beats.speak: Relax. Earth is slowing down, but tides only add one point seven milliseconds to the day every century.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

caption: If Earth stopped spinning, everything on it would keep moving. Earth is 40,075 km around the equator and turns once every 23.93 hours, so the equator moves at 1,674 km/h (465 m/s, faster than sound). The air would keep going too: 4.1 times the strongest gust ever measured (408 km/h, Barrow Island, 1996). At 45 degrees north it is 1,184 km/h, at the North Pole 0. Do not worry: tides only add about 1.7 milliseconds to the day each century.
notes: NASA Earth fact sheet: equatorial radius 6378.137 km, sidereal rotation 23.9345 h. Physics Classroom: sound 343 m/s at 20 C. Guinness/WMO: 408 km/h gust, Barrow Island, 10 Apr 1996, ratified 2010. Space.com (Andrew Layden, BGSU): in a stopped Earth days and nights would each last about six months. Scientific American: tides add 1.7 ms to the day each century. All derived values from whatif.py stats.
